item.title: US targets Africa’s critical minerals to counter rivals
item.description: In 2026, the United States went on an economic offensive looking to access critical minerals across Africa in its race to compete with China for materials that are essential for new technologies and the energy transformation. But it was the strategic partnership agreed in December 2025 with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) that illustrated Washington’s economic push to secure its supply of critical minerals and reduce dependence on China. China has had a long head-start. It began investing in the African mining sector in the 1990s. The deal stipulated that Kinshasa would identify a portfolio of mining assets on which American investors have a right of first offer. Zimbabwe suspended exports of raw minerals in February, ahead of a total ban in 2027, saying it would require processing and transformation to take place in the country. The ban prompted mining companies to rush to build lithium processing plants, the first step in the value chain. A first factory, built by a Chinese company, is now operational. Others are planned. The DRC, the world’s leading cobalt producer, has suspended exports of the metal needed for top-range batteries from next month. The measure, which aims to shore up prices by preventing an over-supply on the market, had already been applied in February 2025 before a quota policy was introduced. “Our country has for a long time contributed to the wealth of industries around the world without keeping a sufficient amount of the added value to ensure its own economic transition,” Congolese President Felix Tshisekedi told a business conference in Kinshasa this week. In remarks to companies and banks at the same forum, Mines Minister Louis Watum assured “those who will carry out processing on our soil will find a partner in the government”. – Banking on rail? – Interest in the continent’s mineral resources has led to the implementation and completion of several major infrastructure projects. The goal of schemes such as Guinea’s large-scale Simandou iron ore mining project or the Lobito Corridor between the DRC and Angola is to secure and speed up the transportation of minerals to port, often by rail. While some of the mining output from the southern DRC is still transported in a constant stream of trucks to South African ports, another part now goes by rail to the Angolan port of Lobito on the Atlantic coast. Zambia is also involved in the EU- and US-financed Lobito project. So far, it has been the missing link but progress is expected in 2027 on a railway line project connecting the copper-producing region in the north to the existing line in Angola. – High-risk? – In some African countries, US investors remain cautious and demand guarantees to secure their investments. Talks are under way between the United States and the DRC in particular to improve the business climate in a country perceived as risky due to endemic corruption, an unpredictable tax system and weak legal protection. “Kinshasa expects concrete investments in 2027. But major changes should not be expected too quickly because mining projects take time,” Jacques Mukena, of the Ebuteli institute, said. The eastern conflict pitting armed anti-governmental forces backed by Rwanda against the Congolese army also continues, despite several mediation efforts. “Without progress on security, investors will remain cautious,” Mukena said. item.title: How OBJ stopped Gaddafi’s AK-47 convoy at Abuja airport in 2006 – Fani-Kayode
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode, has disclosed how former President Olusegun Obasanjo refused to let assassinated Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi’s delegation bring high-powered weapons into Abuja in 2006, a decision he said saved lives. Fani-Kayode, a former minister of aviation, gave the account in a Facebook post titled “20 Years Ago With Muammar Ghaddafi!” who had then arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit. The boot of each of those cars was filled with AK-47s and all manner of sophisticated weapons,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the convoy was blocked at the gate by Nigerian security personnel and the military. He said Gaddafi, members of his delegation and even his bodyguards would be allowed in with their sidearms, but not the weapons in the boots of the vehicles. item.title: Musk To Give Two SpaceX Shares To ‘Every Child In America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. The world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year. He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work. APRIL 30: Elon Musk arrives to court at the Ronald V. Dellums Federal Building on April 30, 2026 in Oakland, California. (Photo by Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP “I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.” “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said. In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.” There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau. The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion. SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk’s ambition to colonize Mars. item.title: 2027: ADC’s Babba Kaita Rallies Katsina Voters, Promises LG Autonomy, Anti-Corruption Drive
item.description: The Katsina State Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) for the 2027 general elections, Senator Ahmad Babba Kaita, has described the forthcoming polls as a crucial battle that Nigerians must pursue with determination and collective strength. Senator Kaita made the declaration while continuing his campaign tour across the Funtua Zone, where he sought the support and confidence of voters ahead of the 2027 elections. Addressing supporters during the campaign engagements, the former federal lawmaker said only Nigerians who are directly affected by governance challenges can fully explain the difficulties facing the country, arguing that the electorate has the power to determine the direction of the nation through their votes. According to him, the growing enthusiasm witnessed during ADC campaigns, including those led by the party’s presidential candidate and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, demonstrates Nigerians’ desire for a new political direction. Kaita said the reception accorded the ADC across the country, including Katsina State, shows that citizens are prepared to use the ballot box to pursue what he described as positive change. The ADC governorship candidate also disclosed that candidates of the party from the seven North-West states have agreed to implement a common development agenda focused on tackling insecurity, improving education, boosting agriculture, strengthening healthcare delivery, expanding economic opportunities and promoting social development. On his plans for Katsina State, Senator Kaita reiterated his commitment to granting full autonomy to local government areas within his first six months in office if elected. He said his administration would conduct local government elections within the first three months, describing grassroots governance as a critical foundation for effective development. However, Kaita warned that local government administrations and other government institutions under his leadership would be subjected to strict monitoring to prevent abuse and mismanagement of public resources. “We will establish a state-owned Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) that will ensure the judicious management of our resources for the benefit of the people of Katsina State,” he assured. In a statement issued by the Spokesman of Kaita, the ADC campaign train is currently touring the 11 local government areas of Funtua Zone, attracting large crowds of supporters across towns and villages. The statement said residents, including youths, women and community leaders, have continued to welcome the campaign team with prayers, endorsements and assurances of support as the party intensifies its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections. Senator Kaita made the declaration while continuing his campaign tour across the Funtua Zone, where he sought the support and confidence of voters ahead of the 2027 elections. Addressing supporters during the campaign engagements, the former federal lawmaker said only Nigerians who are directly affected by governance challenges can fully explain the difficulties facing the country, arguing that the electorate has the power to determine the direction of the nation through their votes. According to him, the growing enthusiasm witnessed during ADC campaigns, including those led by the party’s presidential candidate and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, demonstrates Nigerians’ desire for a new political direction. Kaita said the reception accorded the ADC across the country, including Katsina State, shows that citizens are prepared to use the ballot box to pursue what he described as positive change. The ADC governorship candidate also disclosed that candidates of the party from the seven North-West states have agreed to implement a common development agenda focused on tackling insecurity, improving education, boosting agriculture, strengthening healthcare delivery, expanding economic opportunities and promoting social development. On his plans for Katsina State, Senator Kaita reiterated his commitment to granting full autonomy to local government areas within his first six months in office if elected. He said his administration would conduct local government elections within the first three months, describing grassroots governance as a critical foundation for effective development. However, Kaita warned that local government administrations and other government institutions under his leadership would be subjected to strict monitoring to prevent abuse and mismanagement of public resources. “We will establish a state-owned Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) that will ensure the judicious management of our resources for the benefit of the people of Katsina State,” he assured. In a statement issued by the Spokesman of Kaita, the ADC campaign train is currently touring the 11 local government areas of Funtua Zone, attracting large crowds of supporters across towns and villages. The statement said residents, including youths, women and community leaders, have continued to welcome the campaign team with prayers, endorsements and assurances of support as the party intensifies its mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections. item.title: #EndSARS: Court gives hospital 14 days to release Onifade’s remains
item.description: By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State District Coroner, Mrs Temitope Oladele, has ordered the Infectious Diseases Hospital (IDH), Yaba, Lagos, to release the remains of late journalist, Pelumi Onifade, to his parents within 14 days for burial. The order was issued during the ongoing inquest into the death of the Gboah TV reporter, who was reportedly shot during the #EndSARS protests in October 2020 and subsequently died in police custody. Oladele granted the application by the family’s counsel, Alimi Adamu, who also represents Media Rights Agenda, MRA, following six years of retention of the deceased’s remains at the hospital. The coroner directed that the remains, identified by tag number 1385, be released to the family within 14 days of the hospital receiving the order. The inquest also issued fresh witness summons to persons considered crucial to establishing the circumstances surrounding Onifade’s shooting, arrest and death. The proceedings followed a July 19, 2024 judgment of the Federal High Court in Lagos, which directed the Lagos State Attorney-General to investigate Onifade’s death, conduct a coroner’s inquest and identify and prosecute those responsible. At the latest sitting, Adamu told the court that efforts to secure the attendance of a witness reportedly present when Onifade was killed had been unsuccessful. He said the witness could provide important evidence about the journalist’s arrest and subsequent disappearance but was apprehensive about appearing in court. Adamu urged the coroner to allow the witness to testify electronically, with measures to protect his identity. The court approved the application for the summons to be served through WhatsApp. Another witness, Jimmy Michael, reportedly with Onifade at the time of the shooting, was also summoned. Counsel to the Lagos State Attorney-General, Adebola Araba, told the court that Michael had explained that his Christmas business engagements prevented him from attending, but he had not refused to participate in the inquest. The court equally identified Gboah TV Director, Michael Oluwajoba Bamiro, as a relevant witness, approving his appearance at the next sitting. Onifade’s mother, Bose, also adopted her witness statement on oath, filed on November 11, 2026, which the court admitted in evidence. Adamu urged the coroner to record that the remains had been kept in state custody for forensic and judicial purposes to facilitate administrative arrangements, including issues relating to storage fees. The inquest was adjourned until December 15, 2026, for further proceedings. The post #EndSARS: Court gives hospital 14 days to release Onifade’s remains appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Iyabo Ojo apologises over viral handshake video
item.description: Nollywood actress, Iyabo Ojo, has apologised following a viral video showing a man appearing to decline her handshake at an event, explaining that she was unaware he was a traditional ruler. The actress addressed the controversy in a statement posted on her Instagram page, saying she had approached the table after being informed that some people seated there had sent greetings to her. Ojo said she recognised HRM Oloto, whom she described as her brother, and assumed the other people at the table were his friends. “I was sitting pretty when someone came to tell me they sent their greetings from that table. When I looked in that direction and saw HRM Oloto, I said, ‘Ah, okay, that’s my brother, let me go greet him,’” she said. “Honestly, I am very sorry if I caused any offence. I meant no disrespect to his throne and culture. Henceforth, I will be very mindful,” she stated. Ojo also acknowledged that she was accustomed to greeting people with handshakes and hugs, noting that she had been making efforts to change the habit. “We learn every day. I meant no disrespect. item.title: US lists 63 professions eligible for 3-year work visa
item.description: The US has outlined 63 professional categories whose qualified practitioners can apply for a temporary work visa allowing them to take up employment in the country for up to three years. The arrangement, known as the Trade National (TN) visa, is available exclusively to citizens of Canada and Mexico under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). The TN visa allows eligible professionals from the two neighbouring countries to work for US employers in specified occupations, provided they meet the educational, professional and employment requirements attached to their chosen fields. According to the US Department of State, applicants must be citizens of either Canada or Mexico, have a profession recognised under the USMCA list, secure a prearranged job with a US employer and possess the qualifications required for the position. The list covers several professional sectors, including healthcare, engineering, science, education, accounting and other specialised occupations. Some of the professions recognised under the arrangement include accountants, architects, engineers, lawyers, pharmacists, registered nurses, dentists, veterinarians, economists, mathematicians, scientists, university lecturers and computer systems analysts. Other eligible occupations include agriculturalists, biologists, chemists, geologists, meteorologists, psychologists, social workers, urban planners and technical publications writers. However, appearing on the list does not automatically guarantee approval, as applicants must demonstrate that they satisfy the specific educational or professional requirements for their occupations. Most of the listed professions require a bachelor’s degree or its equivalent, although some categories permit alternative qualifications or professional credentials. The US government also requires applicants to provide details of their proposed employment, including their job responsibilities, expected duration of stay, qualifications and remuneration arrangements. Under Section 214.6 of Title 8 of the US Code of Federal Regulations, successful TN applicants can be admitted into the country for a period not exceeding three years. The classification can also be extended, subject to the applicant continuing to meet the relevant requirements. The application process differs slightly between the two eligible nationalities. item.title: ‘We will find a way to win’ insists Pochettino after rocky Man Utd start
item.description: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino insisted his team would find a way to win games after a tricky start to life at the helm of the Red Devils. United were held to a chaotic 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, after a 4-0 thrashing by rivals Liverpool in his first match on Sunday. Man United, 19th in the Premier League, were upset with several refereeing decisions across both matches, but Pochettino said his team had to take responsibility for their situation. “I’m happy to be here,” said Pochettino, when asked about the various decisions that had gone against his team in his first week in charge. “We are here to take responsibility… we are going for sure to improve and to put that team in the place that, because of their history, we deserve to be. “Nothing is easy but we have the energy and I think we have the capacity, and most importantly the players and the power and the energy from our fans that is massive and I think united, all together, I think we will find a way to perform and win games.” United had two goals controversially ruled out against Sporting, but might have won the game were it not for a mistake from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. item.title: Dangote Refinery shares to trade on NGX December 1
item.description: Shares of Dangote Petroleum Refinery will begin trading on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) on December 1, the company has announced. Devakumar Edwin, Vice-President, Oil and Gas, Dangote Group, disclosed the development on Wednesday, according to a Reuters report. The listing will follow the refinery’s initial public offering (IPO), which attracted significant investor interest and was heavily oversubscribed. The development comes after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the refinery’s plan to allocate shares to investors, paving the way for the completion of the offer and its stock market debut. Dangote Refinery had sought to increase the size of its IPO by up to 30 per cent to approximately $2.1 billion following strong demand from investors. On September 11, Aliko Dangote, President of Dangote Industries Limited, said the refinery planned to list on a United States stock exchange after expanding its production capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day within the next two and a half years. However, on November 8, Dangote disclosed that the refinery’s IPO fell short of its target of attracting 10 million investors. Despite missing the target, the industrialist said the offer attracted “millions of investors”. He described the level of participation as significant when compared with some of the largest public offerings in Africa and other parts of the world. item.title: Rewane projects 4.5% growth, urges investors to rethink strategies
item.description: By Onome Onyeme The Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company, Bismarck Rewane, has projected Nigeria’s economic growth at between 4.3 and 4.5 per cent in 2027, urging investors to rethink traditional investment strategies and embrace emerging opportunities. Speaking at the 23rd edition of the Alpha Morgan Economic Review, held virtually yesterday, Rewane said changing economic realities, technological innovation and evolving business models were reshaping investment decisions globally. “The rules of the past are no longer the rules of the present, definitely not the rules of the future,” he said, urging investors to embrace innovation, research and emerging industries rather than rely on past market performance. Rewane, who examined global economic developments and Nigeria’s investment outlook, said businesses and investors that failed to adapt to changing realities risked losing relevance. He cited the evolution of global businesses, including Apple, as examples of how innovation and leadership could determine corporate fortunes, stressing that past success was no guarantee of future dominance. Rewane observed increasing participation in the capital market, with more companies raising funds through the market rather than relying solely on commercial bank loans. However, he warned of possible property market bubble risks, particularly amid the rapid expansion of construction and property investments in Lagos. Rewane projected that some companies could record revenue growth of between 25 and 40 per cent, driven by capital investment, expansion and increased operations across Africa. He also projected the Naira to trade between N1,500 and N1,600 per dollar in 2027, while anticipating an end to global interest rate increases. He clarified that the projections represented his personal assessment of economic developments. Meanwhile, a wave of unrest among high school students will force those vying for the presidency to take a stance on the state of the education system and public services. With far-right candidate Marine Le Pen leading the polls and radical-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon currently projected to advance to the second round, the right and the centre parties are discussing the possibility of a primary. The social-democratic left has held a primary, which was won by Raphael Glucksmann, currently a member of the European parliament. item.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. item.title: CBN raises BDC’s dollar cash limit to $1m weekly
item.description: Banks to receive dollar cash from apex bank to meet demand By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has temporarily raised the weekly dollar cash purchase limit for Bureau De Change (BDC) operators from $150,000 to $1 million, as part of measures to address seasonal demand pressures in the foreign exchange market. The apex bank also pledged to supply authorised dealer banks with dollar cash to meet the requirements of their BDC customers, allowing licensed operators to access up to 100 per cent of their foreign exchange purchases in cash. The development was confirmed by bankers and forex dealers who spoke to Vanguard, following an email communication from the CBN on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, outlining the new operational arrangements. Kunle Ezun, Chief Economist, Ecobank Nigeria, confirmed the development, saying: “Very correct. The message was sent yesterday. The banks are putting machinery in place to commence the sale. Obi and Kwankwaso offered words of comfort and solidarity to the grieving family. Absent from the visit was Omo-Agege. However, Mrs. Umukoro later confirmed to Vanguard in a telephone conversation that the senator later called her to express his condolences. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries.
